gamma_cross_gamma_matrix.text: `theta_time_decay` answers "how much does a single Black-Scholes option's value change as calendar time passes?" It returns Theta per year from `spot`, `strike`, `rate`, `sigma`, `tau`, plus optional `option_type` and `div_yield`. `gamma_cross_gamma_matrix` answers a different question: "how does a portfolio's value respond to price moves in its underlyings, beyond the first-order effect?" It assembles a symmetric matrix from `own_gammas` (the diagonal) and optional `cross_gammas` (the off-diagonals), and gamma P&L for a shock vector `ds` is 0.5 · ds' G ds. In short, `theta_time_decay` is about time and one option, while `gamma_cross_gamma_matrix` is about price shocks across a portfolio. The matrix function also takes gammas you already have, rather than pricing inputs.

explain.text: `theta_time_decay` (Theta Time Decay) computes the Black-Scholes Theta of a European option, which is how much its value changes as calendar time passes, expressed per year. It is defined as −∂V/∂τ, so it measures the effect of the option moving closer to maturity. You provide `spot`, `strike`, `rate`, `sigma` and `tau`, and optionally `option_type` ("call" or "put", defaulting to call) and `div_yield` for a continuous dividend yield. It uses separate call and put formulas that include the dividend yield term, and pyvar does the calculation for you.

when.text:
Use Theta Time Decay (`theta_time_decay`) when you want to see how a Black-Scholes option's value changes as calendar time passes, with everything else held fixed.

- You hold a call or put (set with `option_type`) and want its time decay, quoted per year.
- You're studying how `tau`, `sigma`, `rate` or `div_yield` change the decay profile of a single option.
- You need the Greek for a European-style option priced under Black-Scholes assumptions, with a continuous dividend yield if relevant.
- You're checking the cost of carrying an option position as maturity approaches.
- For how delta itself shifts as maturity nears, `charm_delta_decay` is listed as the sensitivity of delta to time to maturity.
